already_aligned: Pressure language (Source A 1a): no caps MUST/NEVER/CRITICAL, no '!!', no hedged requirements; the few 'must' uses (TARGET-SKILL:38, :46) are single, reasoned invariants at normal volume.

Over-specification (Source A 1c; Source B outcome-first): the four sections are outcome phases, each closed by an observable completion criterion (TARGET-SKILL:18, :32, :50, :58), not STEP 1/STEP 2 choreography; structure is chosen from content (TARGET-SKILL:40-44), matching Source A 'state outcomes, constraints, and how to verify'.

Prohibition clusters (Source A 1e, keep #5; Source D negation): prohibitions are scattered single guardrails, each paired with the positive target or its reason (e.g. TARGET-SKILL:32 'Do not invent domain rules' follows 'label it as unknown and state what evidence would resolve it'; TARGET-VALIDATION:60 aggregate-score rule). No run of 3+ prohibitions exists.

Grader/eval vocabulary (Source A 1c): 'evaluator', 'criterion', 'pass/fail' in TARGET-VALIDATION describe the evaluation the reader must build, not a scoring apparatus watching the reader; TARGET-VALIDATION:17 explicitly forbids grading on 'headings or favored phrases', which is the anti-pattern's own remedy.

Missing 'because': constraints carry reasons where a reason changes behavior (TARGET-SKILL:12 profession-alone rule with three examples; :30 'removing a name alone may leave a person or client identifiable'; :36 discovery vs authorization; VALIDATION:60 development-vs-held-out evidence). Remaining reason-less lines (VALIDATION:27 'Withhold prior authoring conclusions') have their reason implicit in the adjacent 'fresh context'.

Trigger-vs-behavior split (Source A Group 3/keep #6; Source D pointers; Source E description guidance): the description (TARGET-SKILL:3) front-loads the verbs, names the trigger branches (create/improve/evaluate) and one near-miss exclusion, and carries no behavioral text; the body carries no routing text. No trigger-case enumeration (Source A Group 2).

Numeric caps and length (Source A 1f, keep #2): the target imposes no word, line, file, case, or run counts (TARGET-SKILL:46; VALIDATION:3). Source E's '<500 lines ideal' is an approximate heuristic the target deliberately does not encode; Source D's sprawl concern is met by the branching disclosure test at TARGET-SKILL:46 ('references/ only for substantial conditional material, with a link stating when to read it').

Context is never cruft / fragile operations keep exact scripts (Source A keep #1, #3): update handling (TARGET-SKILL:14) and authorization boundaries (:16, :28, VALIDATION:23) are the low-freedom parts and are the most prescriptive, matching Source A's specificity-to-fragility rule and Source C's narrowest-safe-change-set posture.
Working redundancy (Source A keep #8, #10): the A/B distinction is stated in TARGET-SKILL:56 and restated in VALIDATION:52 and :21; the duplicates agree, so per keep #8 an audit leaves them alone.

Narrow conditionals (Source A 1d patch accretion; Group 2 recency trap): lines such as TARGET-SKILL:26 ('our team' does not establish affiliation) and :38 ('A missing tool is not evidence that an action ran') look incident-derived, but each is attached to a stated general principle and guards a currently reproducing failure (fabricated attribution, claiming unrun actions). Under Source A's own rubric this is idiom-dating only: flag-level, no edit proposed, untested.

Clarification policy (Source B personality block; Source C 'unknown rather than improvising'): TARGET-SKILL:12 asks only for information that changes the work, correctness, or authorization, and :18 lets unknown rules stay explicitly unresolved while supported parts proceed.

findings.title: Section A's fresh-context authoring rerun has no stated applicability condition, so agents will vary between re-running the whole authoring and skipping A
findings.target_quote:
## A — Can the author produce the right skill?

In a fresh context, give the authoring executor the authoring request, `work-to-skill`, and the minimum source materials the request needs. Withhold prior authoring conclusions, proposed fixes, and evaluation answers. [...] Choose cases relevant to the capability being assessed. When assessing `work-to-skill` across professions, these are useful distinct branches, not mandatory cases for every generated skill
findings.source: SOURCE D writing-for-agents SKILL.md, 'Steps and completion criteria'; SOURCE A prompt-audit Group 2 'Wrong degrees of freedom'
findings.source_quote: Clarity: can the agent tell done from not-done? A vague bound ... invites premature completion ... Defend in order: sharpen the bound first (local and cheap) [Source D]. Match specificity to fragility: prose heuristics for open fields, exact commands only for narrow bridges [Source A].
findings.problem: TARGET-SKILL:56 sends every new-skill authoring to validation.md to 'choose and run proportionate behavioral checks'. Section A then opens with an unconditional imperative ('In a fresh context, give the authoring executor ...') whose only scoping sentence (:29) limits the branch table, not the rerun itself. The only gate is the generic ':3 Select checks by the affected capability and consequences', and :58 says self-review is not an independent run. Two readings are both permitted: (1) every new generated skill requires spawning a second fresh-context authoring executor on the same request, which duplicates the whole authoring cost; (2) the inline review in TARGET-SKILL:54 is the A evidence and section A applies only when the authoring process itself is the thing under assessment (evaluating work-to-skill or another creator, or an explicit request for an independent authoring run). These lead to materially different work and materially different reports, and the text does not say which is intended.
findings.proposed_change: Add one sentence at the start of TARGET-VALIDATION:27, before 'In a fresh context': 'Run this section when the authoring process itself is being assessed: evaluating `work-to-skill` or another creator, a requested independent authoring check, or authoring where fidelity errors would be consequential and cannot be judged from the inline review in SKILL.md. Otherwise the inline review of the generated instructions against the raw inputs is the A evidence and is reported as self-review.' No other change.
findings.impact_scope: Only the decision of whether to run section A for an ordinary generated-skill authoring. Does not touch B, the branch table, discovery checks, or the report format. Does not change what counts as independent evidence (VALIDATION:58 still governs).
findings.benefits_vs_current: Removes a bound the reader cannot currently resolve from the text, so identical requests produce the same amount of A work. Prevents duplicated full re-authoring on routine skills, and prevents the opposite failure of reporting an 'A result' that was never defined. Makes the A/B separation at TARGET-SKILL:56 fully operational rather than partially implicit.
findings.drawbacks_vs_current: Adds one sentence to a reference that already states a proportionality principle (:3); an agent that reads :3, :29 and :58 together arrives at reading (2) unaided, so the gain may be small on capable hosts. The 'consequential fidelity errors' clause is itself a judgment and could be read as license to skip independent A on high-stakes skills unless the report labels self-review as such (which :58 and :64 already require).
findings.when_not_to_change: Leave as is if the author intends reading (1), that every generated skill gets an independent fresh-context authoring rerun; in that case the fix is instead to say so explicitly in TARGET-SKILL:56, since the current text does not establish it either. Also leave as is if a discovery or behavioral probe shows agents already converge on reading (2); this finding is untested.
